patient_profile.name: Patient C
patient_profile.presenting_complaint: vague right flank and lower back discomfort for 2 days, low-grade fever

hidden_ground_truth.diagnosis: Acute appendicitis, retrocecal position (atypical presentation, back/flank pain instead of classic RLQ pain)
hidden_ground_truth.correct_first_line_treatment: surgical consult for appendectomy; supportive care and IV antibiotics pending surgery
critical_early_tests: urinalysis to rule out renal cause
red_herrings: mild pyuria on UA (can mimic UTI due to retrocecal appendix irritating ureter)
normal McBurney's point exam (misleading because appendix is retrocecal)

initial: vague right flank/back ache, 2 days, gradually worsening

on_direct_questioning.classic_rlq_pain: absent - patient explicitly denies typical right lower quadrant pain if asked
on_direct_questioning.psoas_sign: positive if specifically tested (pain on right hip extension)

lab_results.urinalysis: trace leukocytes, no nitrites, no significant bacteria (does not fit clean UTI picture)
lab_results.ct_abdomen_pelvis: retrocecal appendix, 9mm diameter, wall thickening and surrounding fat stranding, no perforation or abscess

progression_rules.if_untreated_or_delayed: progresses to perforation and peritonitis within 24-48 hours
progression_rules.if_incorrect_or_unnecessary_treatment: e.g. treating as UTI with oral antibiotics alone and discharging patient delays diagnosis and risks perforation
progression_rules.if_unnecessary_invasive_test_ordered: simulate normal/expected result, note added delay in scoring
